text:
Dylan Strome is doing what he usually does, setting people up, and getting less than usual for it at the other end. He has 16 points in 19 games, 13 of them assists, with three goals on 6.0 expected. That gap is one of the bigger ones on the Capitals, and his own shot quality is up from last season (1.09 expected goals per 60 after 0.78). Goals tend to follow chances like that.

His teammates haven't been finishing with him either: Washington has scored 4.7 fewer goals than expected with Strome on the ice. Put both together and his points are, if anything, a little light. The Capitals have dropped three straight, and his last goals came in a two-goal night against Buffalo on Oct. 24.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 98th percentile among forwards for primary shot assists last season, one of the best passers in the league by that measure. Evolving-Hockey flagged the cost: opponents created more with him on (bottom 4% of forwards). That trade-off is the player.
